From ebacb81273599555a7a19f7754a1451206a5fc4f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Lukas Czerner <lczerner@redhat.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2018 14:51:46 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] fuse: fix use-after-free in fuse_direct_IO()

In async IO blocking case the additional reference to the io is taken for
it to survive fuse_aio_complete(). In non blocking case this additional
reference is not needed, however we still reference io to figure out
whether to wait for completion or not. This is wrong and will lead to
use-after-free. Fix it by storing blocking information in separate
variable.

This was spotted by KASAN when running generic/208 fstest.

Signed-off-by: Lukas Czerner <lczerner@redhat.com>
Reported-by: Zorro Lang <zlang@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>
Fixes: 744742d692e3 ("fuse: Add reference counting for fuse_io_priv")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v4.6

diff --git a/fs/fuse/file.c b/fs/fuse/file.c
index cc2121b37bf5..b52f9baaa3e7 100644
--- a/fs/fuse/file.c
+++ b/fs/fuse/file.c
@@ -2924,10 +2924,12 @@ fuse_direct_IO(struct kiocb *iocb, struct iov_iter *iter)
 	}
 
 	if (io->async) {
+		bool blocking = io->blocking;
+
 		fuse_aio_complete(io, ret < 0 ? ret : 0, -1);
 
 		/* we have a non-extending, async request, so return */
-		if (!io->blocking)
+		if (!blocking)
 			return -EIOCBQUEUED;
 
 		wait_for_completion(&wait);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `fs/fuse/file.c`**
- A new boolean variable `blocking` is introduced to store the blocking state of the `io` object.
- The condition that checks if the `io` is blocking has been modified to use the new `blocking` variable instead of directly referencing `io->blocking`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification addresses a use-after-free bug in the `fuse_direct_IO()` function by separating the blocking state into its own variable. This change ensures that the reference to `io` is not misused in the non-blocking case, which could lead to accessing freed memory. By storing the blocking information separately, the code becomes clearer and avoids the risk of incorrect reference counting, thus enhancing the stability of the asynchronous I/O operations.

        Root cause:
        The bug arises from the incorrect handling of the `io` reference in the `fuse_direct_IO()` function when dealing with non-blocking asynchronous I/O operations. Specifically, the code was using the `io->blocking` reference directly to determine whether to wait for completion, which could lead to a use-after-free situation if the `io` object was freed before this check was completed. This was particularly problematic in the non-blocking case where the additional reference to `io` was not taken, leading to potential access of freed memory.
